members.name: nifty_intraday_momentum_factor_v1
members.thesis: Cross-sectional intraday momentum: stocks that outperformed in the first 90 minutes continue to outperform for the next 90 minutes, and vice versa. This is driven by institutional order-splitting — a large buy order in the morning continues executing through the afternoon. The inefficiency exists be
weaknesses: 10 simultaneous positions at Zerodha = ₹400+ brokerage per day. Need consistent edge to justify the fixed cost overhead.
Morning momentum can reverse at exactly the entry time (10:45) due to profit-taking. The 90-min lookback is arbitrary.
Long/short construction is imperfect — NIFTY 50 is not truly market-neutral when you're long top 5 and short bottom 5. Sector concentration risk.
members.prior_art: Intraday cross-sectional momentum. Academic: Gao et al. (2018) on intraday momentum patterns. Also: Jegadeesh/Titman adapted to intraday.

members.name: factor_momentum_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 100 constituents grouped by GICS sector
members.thesis: Academic factor investing (value + momentum) works at monthly frequencies but is under-explored intraday. Stocks that are relatively cheap (low P/E within sector) AND showing strong intraday momentum (top quartile of 60-min returns) tend to outperform in the subsequent 30-60 minutes. The inefficienc
filters: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for momentum calc) or after 15:00
Stock volume in last 60 bars > 50th percentile of its 20-day avg
Sector index for the stock must not be down > 2% from previous close
weaknesses: PE ratio is a daily/quarterly metric — using it for intraday decisions mixes time horizons awkwardly; PE does not change intraday, so value rank is static for the session
Cross-sectional ranking requires real-time computation across sector peers, adding latency; if a sector has only 5-6 liquid names, ranks are noisy
60-bar momentum lookback delays signals — by the time a stock reaches top quintile momentum, the move may be 50-70% complete, limiting remaining upside
members.prior_art: Fama-French factor models; Asness et al. (2013) 'Value and Momentum Everywhere'; Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) momentum; intraday factor application is novel but built on established theory

members.name: quality_momentum_v1
members.thesis: High-quality companies (high ROE, low debt/equity, consistent earnings) that also exhibit strong intraday momentum are less likely to experience sharp reversals compared to low-quality momentum stocks. The quality filter acts as crash protection — high ROE, low-leverage names attract institutional b
filters: India VIX < 25; skip short entries if VIX < 12 (low-vol bullish regime)
NIFTY 50 direction must agree with trade direction (NIFTY EMA(9) vs EMA(21))
weaknesses: Quality filter is static (changes quarterly) — cannot adapt to rapid deterioration in company fundamentals; a company may report bad results tomorrow while still appearing high-quality today
Asymmetric long/short logic (long quality, short junk) creates directional bias — net long in bull markets, which may not be the strategy's intent
EMA(9)/EMA(21) crossover on 1-min bars generates frequent whipsaws; requires momentum confirmation to filter but still produces false signals in choppy markets
members.prior_art: Novy-Marx (2013) on quality factor; Asness et al. 'Quality Minus Junk'; momentum factor (Jegadeesh-Titman); quality-momentum combination explored in AQR research papers
